issue_context.title: Add axis argument to DataFrame.corr
issue_context.body:
#### Location of the documentation

https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.corr.html

#### Documentation problem

How should I get the correlation among the rows? I can obviously do `df.T.corr()` but this strikes me as a workaround rather than a nice way to do things. I wrote a `df.corr(axis=1)` assuming that would work. Curious what people feel is idiomatic, and would recommend some mention in the docs.
comments: You should try asking on StackOverflow where the Q&A format is better served to answer this. This board is reserved for issues and enhancement requests

@WillAyd (I should have mentioned this in my original post:) StackOverflow has an answer recommending df.T.corr(), but although that works I don't think it's idiomatic, and if there's a better way, I think it should be mentioned in the docs. If not, I'm recommending that the .corr() function be updated to take an `axis` keyword argument.
Oh OK I see. Sure let's log as a request for the axis argument then
Also for symmetry would be nice to add to DataFrame.cov

review_comments: I think it's usually encouraged to explicitly write out the expected DataFrame so that `expected` doesn't go down the same code path as `result`

Yeah I could do that but, wouldn't it just be a test for Dataframe.corr function itself. Since the original operations to be done on matrix itself are left unchanged.

Personally I don't think explicitly writing Dataframe in this case is needed, unless (as you suggested) instead of taking a transpose we implement a workaround involving changing the main function itself.
OK sure, perhaps wait for others' comments then

The test comes close to being circular but I think it's probably okay here. In this case it's hard to explicitly construct the expected DataFrame for all methods "from scratch" without either trivial input data or messy juggling of different scipy functions.
don't we have to transpose the results?
I don't think we do since the result is symmetric
can you move this signature to an alias and put it in pandas._typing, cal it MethodWithCallable
put axis labels that are differnt for rows / columns and this should fail (need to handle that)
Can you add a version added directive here? There's an example under ddof for the DataFrame.cov method.
